title: Family Says Laredo Father Died After Nov. 2 Crash; Border Patrol Link Still Unconfirmed
excerpt: Ernesto Quintana, 44, a Laredo father of five, died Nov. 2 after a crash on Santa Maria Avenue. His family believes Border Patrol agents were involved, but investigators have not confirmed a link.
content:
Ernesto Quintana, 44, a Laredo father of five, died on Nov. 2 after a crash on the 800 block of Santa Maria Avenue, and his family believes his death is connected to a Border Patrol operation, according to KGNS.

Quintana was driving his daughter to work that morning, his family told KGNS. They say he called his wife, Norma Quintana, before the crash to say he was being followed by Border Patrol agents. Norma Quintana found him at about 6:30 a.m. and said his heart was still beating; he was later pronounced dead at the hospital.

Family members told KGNS they saw him being followed on security footage. The station said it reviewed footage showing a Border Patrol vehicle driving past his home around 6:20 a.m., but the footage did not show whether an agent was following Quintana.

Whether Border Patrol agents were involved in the crash remains unconfirmed. Investigators have not said whether agents were involved, the Webb County Medical Examiner's Office is waiting on toxicology results, and the family says it is still waiting on the autopsy report. A U.S. Customs and Border Protection spokesperson told KGNS that U.S. Border Patrol does not comment on individual cases at this time. Laredo police have a crash report, but it is unclear whether Border Patrol was involved in the crash, according to KGNS.

KGNS also quoted Border Patrol Chief Mike Banks saying his agents were involved in a pursuit that resulted in a crash, but the station did not tie that statement to a specific date or location, or to Quintana's crash.

The family has hired attorney David Martinez, who is consulting with a death investigations attorney in Corpus Christi. The family is being told it is a federal investigation, and Martinez said he has not been able to obtain the autopsy report, the toxicology report or the report on the scene.

A funeral service for Quintana was scheduled for Nov. 18 at 4 p.m. at the Church of Jesus Christ, 101 N. San Eduardo Ave. in Laredo.

Source: KGNS, Nov. 17, 2026.
